businessRequirements.proposedTitle: TCP/IP TPDU Protocol ID is fixed at 0x60
businessRequirements.proposedRequirement: For the standard BUYPASS TCP/IP header, the one-byte TPDU Protocol ID shall be 0x60.
businessRequirements.notes: Logical-header probes only; full-message transport/wire validation remains separate.

businessRequirements.currentTitle: Reserved TPDU destination and source addresses are zero
businessRequirements.proposedTitle: Reserved TPDU destination and source addresses are zero
businessRequirements.proposedRequirement: In messages sent to BUYPASS, the two-byte TPDU Destination Address and two-byte TPDU Source Address shall each be 0x0000.
businessRequirements.notes: The specification states this for messages to BUYPASS; do not generalize to other transports or peers.

businessRequirements.currentTitle: Declined financial responses carry a decline code
businessRequirements.proposedRequirement: Element 83 is the one-byte Financial Response Code and identifies a financial response as an approval with purchase/capture, approval without purchase/capture, or decline. Keep the separate Element 26 Decline Code distinct.
businessRequirements.notes: Response-family value validation must use the separate Element 83 family matrix; do not treat response code as Element 26.

businessRequirements.currentTitle: Fleet Tag format is 3-byte code plus up to 31-byte data payload
businessRequirements.proposedTitle: Fleet Tag uses a fixed three-byte tag and up to 31 data bytes
businessRequirements.proposedRequirement: Fleet Tag fields 1-5, when applicable, use a three-byte fixed tag followed by zero to 31 data bytes; the source limits these fields to Auth Completion messages when Host Prompts are supported.
businessRequirements.notes: The generic maximum does not replace the per-code maximum in SEG101-R-024.

businessRequirements.currentTitle: Fleet Tag 3-byte code must be one of the 17 codes in the fleet-tag code table
businessRequirements.proposedTitle: Fleet Tag code is one of the 17 source-listed Auth Completion codes
businessRequirements.proposedRequirement: When Host Prompts are supported on an Auth Completion (0220), each three-byte Fleet Tag code shall be one of DLS, DLN, PON, INV, TRP, UNT, TLH, DOB, ZIP, END, MID, VIN, TRA, HUB, TLR, CBA, or VHT.
businessRequirements.notes: This repairs the missing eleven codes in the current partial AI-derived comparison; the source table is the authority.

businessRequirements.currentTitle: Fleet Tag data payload conforms to the per-code format
businessRequirements.proposedTitle: Fleet Tag data obeys the source type and maximum for its tag code
businessRequirements.proposedRequirement: For each Auth Completion Fleet Tag, data shall obey that code's source type and maximum length: DLS an3; DLN an22; PON an31; INV an31; TRP an15; UNT an31; TLH n6; DOB n8; ZIP an9; END an31; MID an31; VIN an17; TRA an15; HUB n9; TLR an15; CBA n6; VHT an10.
businessRequirements.notes: Semantic validation of values such as DOB/state/ZIP remains separate from declared type and length.

businessRequirements.currentTitle: Fuel merchants send both fuel and nonfuel product data
businessRequirements.proposedTitle: Fuel merchants send fuel and nonfuel product data
businessRequirements.proposedRequirement: A fuel merchant shall send both fuel and nonfuel product data in the Product Code Data Segment.
businessRequirements.notes: Comdata exclusion and product/amount reconciliation remain separate rules, not silently included here.

businessRequirements.currentTitle: eWIC does not support Return transactions (absolute prohibition, not a code lookup)
businessRequirements.proposedTitle: eWIC does not support Return transactions
businessRequirements.proposedRequirement: The eWIC transaction flow shall not issue a Return transaction; this is an operation prohibition, not a response-code lookup.
businessRequirements.notes: ATL105 does not define a host decline response for an unsupported Return; do not invent one.

businessRequirements.currentTitle: Retrieval requests use Prompt Code 981, or 996 when retrieving proprietary card data, and allow up to 750 bytes of print data per request
businessRequirements.proposedTitle: Electronic Mail Retrieval uses Prompt Code 981, or 996 for proprietary card data; print data is at most 750 bytes per request
businessRequirements.proposedRequirement: A retrieval request shall use Prompt Code 981; retrieval of proprietary card data shall use 996. Print data shall not exceed 750 bytes per request.
businessRequirements.notes: Byte length is measured on encoded data; complete electronic-mail envelope/response behavior requires its own source-backed rules.

businessRequirements.currentTitle: Submission requests use Prompt Code 995, contain up to 217 bytes of data, and receive a confirmation response
businessRequirements.proposedTitle: Electronic Mail Submission uses Prompt Code 995, at most 217 data bytes, and a receipt confirmation response
businessRequirements.proposedRequirement: A submission request shall use Prompt Code 995, contain no more than 217 data bytes, and receive an Electronic Mail Response confirming receipt.
businessRequirements.notes: The response must be bound to the same request before integration execution; no host behavior is claimed here.

businessRequirements.currentTitle: Merchant settlement cutoff and timezone behavior is approved before certification
businessRequirements.proposedTitle: Settlement cutoff/time-zone approval prerequisite (policy register; not an ATL105 BR)
businessRequirements.proposedRequirement: No source-derived runtime requirement is proposed. Preserve the certification policy prerequisite only in the policy/SME register until the policy owner defines the cutoff, timezone, and approval authority.

blocker.requiredDecision: Approve cutoff/time-zone policy or withdraw the certification gate.

businessRequirements.notes: Do not count this as an ATL105 source-derived BR or AI semantic gap; do not create an execution case without the policy definition.

businessRequirements.currentTitle: MasterCard Enhanced Fleet EMV functionality was, as of the specification's authoring, expected to be enabled in First Data production no earlier than June 2026; until then it is for development/certification preparation only and must not be used in live production transactions
businessRequirements.proposedTitle: MasterCard Enhanced Fleet availability notice (ATL105 2026-3, historical date condition)
businessRequirements.proposedRequirement: The 2026-3 specification states that MasterCard Enhanced functionality was expected in First Data production no earlier than June 2026 and, until enabled, was for development/certification preparation rather than live transactions.

blocker.requiredDecision: Confirm current production enablement, effective date, and environment before deriving a current live-use test.

businessRequirements.notes: Keep the dated source statement; do not infer that the June 2026 milestone occurred.

businessRequirements.currentTitle: Account Updater Result Code (Table 006) is a fixed 6-character code from a documented enumeration (VAU001 through VAU016, non-contiguous — VAU015 absent), applicable only to Visa
businessRequirements.proposedTitle: Visa Account Updater Result Code is a six-character Table 006 value from the source enumeration
businessRequirements.proposedRequirement: When the response field is applicable (Visa and an Account Updater Request Indicator of Y or I), Table 006 has ID 006, length 006, and one of VAU001-VAU014 or VAU016; VAU015 is not defined in the source list.
businessRequirements.notes: Segment 155 has no separators; layout and parent transaction/Segment 111 context need independent fixture coverage.

businessRequirements.currentTitle: Connector Type (Table 12) uses a documented Visa-defined enumeration (001-003, 100-103, 200)
businessRequirements.proposedTitle: Visa EV Connector Type is one of the eight source-defined codes
businessRequirements.proposedRequirement: Connector Type Table 12, when present for the applicable Visa EV charging context, shall use 001, 002, 003, 100, 101, 102, 103, or 200.
businessRequirements.notes: Do not synthesize EV transaction tokens or infer network support beyond the source-defined Visa list.

businessRequirements.currentTitle: A Date and Time Load is initiated by the device with Load Type 'D' (Date and Time Load Request: '?' + Terminal Identifier + 'D'); the merchant load flag does not have to be set, and the response includes adjustments for the initiating device's time zone and daylight saving time
businessRequirements.proposedTitle: Date and Time Load request is device-initiated with Load Type D; response uses initiating-device timezone/DST
businessRequirements.proposedRequirement: The request is the positional string '?' + 13-character Terminal Identifier + 'D', with no Field Separators; no merchant load flag is required. The response time is adjusted for the initiating device's timezone and daylight-saving setting.
businessRequirements.notes: Request serialization is locally source-testable; response clock conversion is not executable without a source-bound timezone fixture.

businessRequirements.currentTitle: Software update processing: a bit on the merchant profile makes BUYPASS return Download Indicator 1 on the next transaction response; the device requests a load; BUYPASS returns DL4 and DL5; the device stores New Software Version, Software Terminal Record ID, Software Load Phone Number or IP/URL Address, Request Date and Request Time; at that date and time the device dials the Software Load Phone Number and requests a full application load; afterwards it requests a Table Load, which BUYPASS sends without the profile bit
businessRequirements.proposedTitle: Software update follows the eight-step profile/download/load/schedule/completion sequence
businessRequirements.proposedRequirement: Follow the source sequence: profile bit; Download Indicator 1 on the next transaction response; Table Load request; DL4/DL5 response; store version/record ID/address/date/time; scheduled full application load; on success request Table Load; BUYPASS sends that Table Load without the profile bit. Automated full-load attempts are limited to three; unsuccessful load prints the decline message.
businessRequirements.notes: No actual application image, network endpoint, device-management response, or production software data is included.
